title: Cadence families: a reader picks one cadence, so nobody gets an item twice
description:
Lists that carry the same items at different cadences (every item, daily summary) form a family. A reader holds at most one list of a family at a time; choosing another moves them. A membership records `since`. A periodic Delivery goes to readers who were members at the period's start; an every-item Delivery goes to members at the moment it is sent. So a reader who moves from every-item to daily at noon gets today's earlier items once (as they happened) and their first summary for the next period. A curated weekly newsletter is its own family and may repeat items by design. Enforced in Caducus's preference write.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A reader cannot hold two lists of one family.
- After switching cadence a reader gets no item twice.
- The weekly newsletter is unaffected by a reader's daily or every-item choice.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- cadence-family.feature: choosing daily removes every-item; a noon switch gets no duplicate; a reader on weekly and daily gets both; the rule holds through the one-click unsubscribe path.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** Caducus: public-audience preference rule (released through the Caducus release path).

**Part of:** Newsletters and subscriptions: weekly, daily and every new item. Slice code N2 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
